I am 53 years old and have worked this land for 40 years. I never went to school, but my hands and eyes know what the soil needs. With 15 mu and only my wife and me to work it, I must be practical and not spread myself too thin. I will keep 10 mu in my wheat-maize rotation, which has fed us reliably for decades. I sowed improved wheat seed last autumn, and now that the growing season has started I will irrigate it four times — the winter irrigation saved it from the cold, and I will add water at green-up, jointing, and grain filling. I apply compound fertilizer as basal and topdress with urea in spring, about 20 kg of nitrogen per mu along with phosphorus and potassium. I will spray three times for weeds and pests. After harvesting wheat in June, I will immediately plant hybrid maize without tilling — there is no time to waste between crops, and no-tillage works fine if the wheat stubble is managed well. The maize needs two irrigations and three pesticide sprays, and with good weather it should yield around 600 kg per mu.

The remaining 5 mu I will plant with hybrid cotton in April. Cotton earns better money but demands more labor and attention. I will rotary till the cotton field and put down fertilizer with more potash for the bolls — about 20 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 7 kg potassium per mu. Cotton must be irrigated three times at budding, flowering, and boll stage, and I will spray pesticides eight times because bollworms and aphids never rest around here. I expect about 280 kg of seed cotton per mu. This is my plan — it is what I have always done, and it works.
